title.narrative: Internews: Support to Moldovan media and innovative media literacy 2020-2022
Internews: Support to Moldovan media and innovative media literacy 2020-2022

description.narrative:
Detta stöd för mediesektorn genom Internews förbereds som ett normalt bidrag. Insatsen syftar till att stödja vissa medier och civilsamhällets organisationer i arbetet med att utveckla intern kapacitet och strategier. Projektet föruäntas fylla en viktig funktion i att stärka den oberoende mediesektorn och civilsamhället.
Insatsens totala budget uppgår till 6 084 907 SEK.

This support for media sector through Internews is prepared as a normal contribution. It aims at supporting some media outlets and civil society organizations to develop its internal capacities and strategies. The project is expected to play an important role in strengthening the independent media sector and civil society.
The interventions' total budget is 6 084 907 SEK.

The overall objective of the Project is promoting the development of an independent, professional media that provides citizens with access to a diversity of perspectives, and to reduce the media sector’s vulnerability to political and financial interests. The objectives, indicators and measures of implementation are described clearly in the Results Framework, Narrative concept and the budget. The design of the activities, and the implementation approach have been developed as a direct result of the organisational capacity assessment conducted by Internews on all key partners in February 2020 with support from Sida and the Media-M project. The activities are structured in the following groups planned to be implemented during 24 months: Activity 1. Media Expertise for Key Partners Internews will provide expert media consultants to four key partners to provide support across various functions. The experts work side-by-side on a daily basis with staff over a long period of time and help them overcome apparent deficiencies. Such targeted and personalised assistance is not possible in the case of more general training that is usually attended by various media professionals representing different outlets. Activity 2. Subgrants schemes 2.1. Subgrants to Key Partners will be awarded to a number of key partners based directly on the results and recommendations of the organisational capacity assessment conducted by Internews. 2.2. Based on recent assessment of the organization, one more partner (additionaly to the group from 2.1) will receive support for improvement of capacity to produce and promote content by upgrading and modernising production equipment and workstations. 2.3. Media Information Gaps Grants Pool - aim to support worthy pilot projects and nascent efforts to develop innovative content offerings so that they become platforms for intelligent and balanced public discussion on issues of national importance. The primary focus of these small grants is to support and enhance media literacy in Moldova. It will address issues including but not limited to the economic, political, and social problems that promote transparency and accountability, and may also impart relevant media literacy information for targeted vulnerable communities.

sector.narrative: Media and free flow of information

description.narrative: The partner organization provided all the reports for 2020 and plans for 2021 in time. The details of implementation process and overview on each beneficiary partner (media outlets), were discussed during annual meting. Supported non-state media outlets developed necessary organisational, editorial, and business plans and strategies. Internews team contracted experts on strategic planning (social media, crowd funding, etc) in this regard and assisted the organizations. Supported non-state media outlets funded crucial staff positions, courses, office rent, and other operational costs and endeavours; acquired necessary equipment, supplies, licenses, and other materials. Tailored mentorship programme was provided to some beneficiaries to improve the editing policy. Media Information Gaps Grants recipients are expected to produce balanced content on media literacy and/or issues of national importance. Even though the pandemic continued to affect the mobility and productivity of reporters, most of the partners adjusted already their style of working. All KPs had to adapt new communication and coordination skills in the hybrid or remote work format. Besides some ethical issues in media during 2021 and challenges with staff at some of the key partners, generally it is assessed as very likely that the objectives of the intervention will be achieved. Overall, there were several major risks that had to be managed during implementation. Internews` approach to managing the risks related to the Covid-19 pandemic was appropriate and effective. By holding sessions online and building in additional time buffers, we were able to ensure the safety of participants and staff while also delivering the project outcomes. The project faced an unexpected risk when the Russian invasion of Ukraine began in February 2022. This event had a significant impact on the operations and workload of all Key Partners. To mitigate this risk, Internews provided emergency support in addition to the support that had already been agreed upon, within the limits of the available budget. The funding partially covered the salaries and financed several editions of newsprint. Additionally, because of the drop in advertising revenue caused by the war, the project covered the office rent for one implementing partner for one month. This emergency support allowed the Key Partners to continue their essential work during a difficult time, ensuring that the project's objectives were still met as much as possible. The unexpected risk highlighted the importance of having contingency plans in place and being able to adapt quickly to changing circumstances.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
